content: 1. A meta-analysis of data from 193,696 participants was conducted and published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine in 2018, volume 52, issue 20, pages 1320-1326. 2. Colpani et al. systematically reviewed and performed a meta-analysis on the impact of lifestyle factors on cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality in middle-aged and elderly women. This study was published in the European Journal of Epidemiology in 2018, volume 33, issue 9, pages 831-845. 3. Del Pozo-Cruz et al. analyzed studies using objective assessments to evaluate the effects of replacing sedentary time with physical activity. Their meta-analysis was published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine in 2018, volume 55, issue 3, pages 395-402. 4. Dinu et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the health outcomes associated with active commuting. This research was published in Sports Medicine in 2019, volume 49, issue 3, pages 437-452. 5. Ekelund et al. examined dose-response relationships between accelerometer-measured physical activity, sedentary time, and all-cause mortality. Their harmonized meta-analysis was published in BMJ in 2019, volume 366, article l4570. 6. Engeroff et al. reviewed the relationship between physical activity across the adult lifespan and domain-specific cognitive function in older adults. This systematic review was published in Sports Medicine in 2018, volume 48, issue 6, pages 1405-1436. 7. Fernandes et al. systematically reviewed the effects of moderate physical exercise on adult cognition. Their findings were published in Frontiers in Physiology in 2018, volume 9, article 667. 8. Flahr et al. reviewed physical activity-based interventions for shift workers, focusing on their health outcomes. This systematic review was published in Preventive Medicine Reports in 2018, pages 323-331. 9. Fuzeki et al. analyzed the health benefits of light-intensity physical activity using accelerometer data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Their systematic review was published in Sports Medicine in 2017, volume 47, issue 9, pages 1769-1793. 10. Gordon et al. conducted a meta-analysis and meta-regression of randomized clinical trials to evaluate the efficacy of resistance exercise training in reducing depressive symptoms. This study was published in JAMA Psychiatry in 2018, volume 75, issue 6, pages 566-576. 11. Gordon et al. also analyzed the effects of resistance exercise training on anxiety through a meta-analysis and meta-regression of randomized controlled trials. This research was published in Sports Medicine in 2017, volume 47, issue 12, pages 2521-2532. 12. Guo and Zhang performed a meta-analysis of prospective studies to investigate the association between ideal cardiovascular health metrics and the risk of cardiovascular events or mortality. Their findings were published in Clinical Cardiology in 2017, volume 40, issue 12, pages 1339-1346. 13. Halloway et al. reviewed the effects of endurance-focused physical activity interventions on brain health. This systematic review was published in Biological Research for Nursing in 2017, pages 53-64. 14. Hart and Buck systematically reviewed and analyzed the impact of resistance training on health-related quality of life in older adults. Their findings were published in Health Promotion Perspectives in 2019, pages 1-12. 15. Herold et al. reviewed the functional and structural brain changes associated with resistance exercises and their cognitive benefits. This systematic review was published in the European Review of Aging and Physical Activity in 2019, volume 16, article 10. 16. Hidayat et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies to assess the influence of physical activity during youth and over a lifetime on the risks of obesity-related cancers. Their findings were published in Nutrition Reviews in 2020, volume 78, issue 1, pages 1-18. 17. Hussenoeder and Riedel-Heller explored the primary prevention of dementia by addressing modifiable risk factors and promoting public brain health. Their review was published in Social Psychiatry and Psychiatric Epidemiology in 2018, pages 1289-1301. 18. Igarashi et al. conducted a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the effects of regular aerobic exercise on blood pressure in East Asians. This study was published in Clinical and Experimental Hypertension in 2018, volume 40, issue 4, pages 378-389. 19. Igarashi et al. also reviewed the required step count for reducing blood pressure through a systematic review and meta-analysis. Their findings were published in the Journal of Human Hypertension in 2018, volume 32, issue 12, pages 814-824. 20. Jiang et al. systematically reviewed and analyzed the effects of Baduanjin exercise on insomnia. Their findings were published in Behavioral Sleep Medicine in 2017, pages 1-13. 21. Kovacevic et al. reviewed the effects of resistance exercise on sleep through a systematic analysis of randomized controlled trials. This study was published in Sleep Medicine Reviews in 2018, volume 39, pages 52-68. 22. Lewis et al. reviewed the role of exercise as a time cue (zeitgeber) for human circadian systems, highlighting its potential to foster health and improve performance. Their findings were published in BMJ Open Sport & Exercise Medicine in 2018, volume 4, issue 1, article e000443. 23. Lipnicki et al. investigated the determinants of cognitive performance and decline across 20 diverse ethno-regional groups in a cohort study. Their findings were published in PLOS Medicine in 2019, volume 16, issue 7, article e1002853. 24. Liu et al. conducted a meta-analysis of cohort studies to examine the association between physical activity and a lower risk of lung cancer. Their findings were published in Frontiers in Oncology in 2019, article 5. 25. Liu et al. also analyzed the relationship between leisure-time physical activity and total and cause-specific mortality in nearly half a million adults in the Asia Cohort Consortium. Their pooled analysis was published in the International Journal of Epidemiology in 2018. 26. Lopez-Valenciano et al. updated a systematic review and meta-analysis on the role of isometric resistance training in managing resting blood pressure in adults. Their findings were published in the Journal of Hypertension in 2019, volume 37, issue 7, pages 1320-1333. 27. Loprinzi and Edwards reviewed the effects of exercise on implicit memory through a brief systematic review. Their findings were published in Psychological Reports in 2018, volume 121, issue 6, pages 1072-1085. 28. Loprinzi et al. reviewed the effects of resistance exercise on episodic memory function. Their findings were published in Clinical Physiology and Functional Imaging in 2018. 29. Loprinzi et al. also reviewed the effects of exercise on memory function among young to middle-aged adults, providing recommendations for future research. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Health Promotion in 2018, volume 32, issue 3, pages 691-704. 30. Lowe et al. systematically reviewed the effects of exercise on sleep in adults with insomnia, including a quality appraisal. Their findings were published in Clinical Psychology Review in 2019, volume 68, pages 1-12.
